arxiv-1705-00293.title: On the Existence of 4-regular Matchstick Graphs
arxiv-1705-00293.creator: Mike Winkler, Peter Dinkelacker, Stefan Vogel
arxiv-1705-00293.description: Abstract A matchstick graph is a planar unit-distance graph. That is a graph drawn with straight edges in the plane such that the edges have unit length, and non-adjacent edges do not intersect. We call a matchstick graph 4-regular if every vertex has only degree 4.

arxiv-2203-09146.title: Resonances and Phase Locking phenomena for foliation preserving torus maps Thanks: Research of X.H. supported by NSFC (NO. 12001148), ZJNSF (NO. LQ21A010013) and HZNU (NO. 2020QDL017) Thanks: Research of R. L. supported in part by NSF DMS18000241
arxiv-2203-09146.creator: Xiaolong He, Rafael de la Llave
arxiv-2203-09146.description: Abstract . It is well known for experts that resonances in nonlinear systems lead to new invariant objects that lead to new behaviors. The goal of this paper is to study the invariant sets generated by resonances under foliation preserving torus maps.

arxiv-2208-10352.title: Dynamical systems analysis of tachyon dark energy model from a new perspective
arxiv-2208-10352.creator: Saddam Hussain, Saikat Chakraborty, Nandan Roy, Kaushik Bhattacharya
arxiv-2208-10352.description: Abstract In this work, we present a new scheme to study the tachyon dark energy model using dynamical systems analysis by considering parametrization of the equation of state(EoS) of the dark energy. Both the canonical and phantom field dynamics are investigated. In our method, we do not require any explicit form of the tachyon potential.

arxiv-2209-02620.title: Three Examples in the Dynamical Systems Theory
arxiv-2209-02620.creator: Mikhail B. SEVRYUK
arxiv-2209-02620.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Mikhail B. SEVRYUK. We present three explicit curious simple examples in the theory of dynamical systems. The first one is an example of two analytic diffeomorphisms R R , S S of a closed two-dimensional annulus that possess the intersection property but their composition R ​ S RS does not ( R R being just the rotation by π / 2 \pi/2 ).

arxiv-2211-04441.title: Double-copy towards supergravity inflation with 𝜶 \bm{\alpha} -attractor models
arxiv-2211-04441.creator: John Joseph M. Carrasco,, Matthew Lewandowski,, and Nicolas H. Pavao
arxiv-2211-04441.description: Abstract Key to the simplicity of supergravity α \alpha -attractor models of inflation are Volkov-Akulov fermions, often in the form of nilpotent superfields. Here we explore the possibility of using the double-copy to construct theories of Dirac-Born-Infeld-Volkov-Akulov (DBIVA) coupled to supergravity.

arxiv-2212-05243.title: Revealing the spectral state transition of the Clocked Burster, GS 1826-238 with NuSTAR StrayCats
arxiv-2212-05243.creator: S. B. Yun, B. W. Grefenstette, R. M. Ludlam, M. C. Brumback, D. J. K. Buisson, G Mastroserio, S. N. Pike
arxiv-2212-05243.description: Abstract We present the long term analysis of GS 1826-238, a neutron star X-ray binary known as the “Clocked Burster”, using data from NuSTAR StrayCats. StrayCats, a catalogue of NuSTAR stray light data, contains data from bright, off-axis X-ray sources that have not been focused by the NuSTAR optics.

arxiv-2212-14519.title: White dwarf binary modulation can help stochastic gravitational wave background search
arxiv-2212-14519.creator: Shijie Lin, Bin Hu, Xue-Hao Zhang, Yu-Xiao Liu
arxiv-2212-14519.description: Abstract For the stochastic gravitational wave backgrounds (SGWBs) search centred at the milli-Hz band, the galactic foreground produced by white dwarf binaries (WDBs) within the Milky Way contaminates the extra-galactic signal severely. Because of the anisotropic distribution pattern of the WDBs and the motion of the spaceborne gravitational wave interferometer constellation, the time-domain data stream will show an annual modulation.

arxiv-2301-03738.title: Hyperbolic summations derived using the Jacobi functions dc and nc
arxiv-2301-03738.description: Abstract We introduce a method that is based on Fourier series expansions related to Jacobi elliptic functions and that we apply to determine new identities for evaluating hyperbolic infinite sums in terms of the complete elliptic integrals K K and E E .

arxiv-2301-04652.title: ESTIMATE DEFORMATION CAPACITY OF NON-DUCTILE RC SHEAR WALLS USING EXPLAINABLE BOOSTING MACHINE
arxiv-2301-04652.creator: Zeynep Tuna Deger (1*), Gulsen Taskin Kaya (1), John W. Wallace (2)
arxiv-2301-04652.description: Abstract Machine learning is becoming increasingly prevalent for tackling challenges in earthquake engineering and providing fairly reliable and accurate predictions. However, it is mostly unclear how decisions are made because machine learning models are generally highly sophisticated, resulting in opaque black-box models.

arxiv-2306-12630.title: On sets of rational functions which locally represent all of ℚ \mathbb{Q}
arxiv-2306-12630.creator: Benjamin Klahn, Joachim König
arxiv-2306-12630.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Benjamin Klahn, Joachim König. We investigate finite sets of rational functions { f 1 , f 2 , … , f r } \{f_{1},f_{2},\dots,f_{r}\} defined over some number field K K satisfying that any t 0 ∈ K t_{0}\in K is a K p K_{p} -value of one of the functions f i f_{i} for almost all primes p p of K K .

arxiv-2402-03990.title: Subsampling is not Magic: Why Large Batch Sizes Work for Differentially Private Stochastic Optimisation
arxiv-2402-03990.creator: Ossi Räisä, Joonas Jälkö, Antti Honkela
arxiv-2402-03990.description: Abstract We study how the batch size affects the total gradient variance in differentially private stochastic gradient descent (DP-SGD), seeking a theoretical explanation for the usefulness of large batch sizes. As DP-SGD is the basis of modern DP deep learning, its properties have been widely studied, and recent works have empirically found large batch sizes to be beneficial.

arxiv-2407-12179.title: A continuous-time fundamental lemma and its application in data-driven optimal control Thanks: P. Schmitz is grateful for the support from the Carl Zeiss Foundation (VerneDCt – Project No. 2011640173). K. Worthmann gratefully acknowledges funding by the German Research Foundation (DFG; project numbe
arxiv-2407-12179.creator: Philipp Schmitz, Timm Faulwasser, Paolo Rapisarda, Karl Worthmann
arxiv-2407-12179.description: Abstract . Data-driven control of discrete-time and continuous-time systems is of tremendous research interest. In this paper, we explore data-driven optimal control of continuous-time linear systems using input-output data. Based on a density result, we rigorously derive error bounds for finite-order polynomial approximations of elements of the system behavior.

arxiv-2501-10013.title: CaFA: Cost-aware, Feasible Attacks With Database Constraints Against Neural Tabular Classifiers
arxiv-2501-10013.creator: Matan Ben-Tov 1 , Daniel Deutch 1 , Nave Frost 2 , and Mahmood Sharif 1
arxiv-2501-10013.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Matan Ben-Tov 1 , Daniel Deutch 1 , Nave Frost 2 , and Mahmood Sharif 1. This work presents CaFA, a system for C ost- a ware F easible A ttacks for assessing the robustness of neural tabular classifiers against adversarial examples realizable in the problem space, while minimizing adversaries’ effort. To this end, CaFA leverages TabPGD---an algorithm we set forth to generate adversarial perturbations suitable for tabular data---and incorporates integrity constraints automatically mined by state-of-the-art database methods.

arxiv-2504-08776.creator: Gautam Kishore Shahi, Oshani Seneviratne, Marc Spaniol
arxiv-2504-08776.description: Abstract . With the shift from traditional to digital media, the online landscape now hosts not only reliable news articles but also a significant amount of unreliable content. Digital media has faster reachability by significantly influencing public opinion and advancing political agendas.

arxiv-2512-24199.title: Gaussian free fields on Hamming graphs and
arxiv-2512-24199.creator: lattice spin systems
arxiv-2512-24199.description: Abstract Abstract. We discuss a class of discrete Gaussian free fields on Hamming graphs, where interactions are determined solely by the Hamming distance between vertices. The purpose of examining this class is that it differs significantly from the commonly discussed spin system on the integer lattice with nearest-neighbour interactions.

plos-pone-0001918.creator: Meltem Muftuoglu, Rika Kusumoto, Elzbieta Speina et al.
plos-pone-0001918.description: PLOS ONE research article. The Werner protein (WRN), defective in the premature aging disorder Werner syndrome, participates in a number of DNA metabolic processes, and we have been interested in the possible regulation of its function in DNA repair by post-translational modifications. Acetylation mediated

pmc-10532267.title: Changes in Oral-Health-Related Quality of Life of Egyptian Children Treated under Dental General Anesthesia: A Prospective Study
pmc-10532267.creator: Mahmoud Faheem, Dalia Moheb, Sherif Bahgat, Christian Splieth, Katrin Bekes, Antonella Polimeni, John Mark Ansermino
pmc-10532267.description: Background: Treatment of young children under dental general anesthesia (DGA) is sometimes necessary due to lack of cooperation and the complexity of dental treatment. The aim of this study was to assess the changes in oral-health-related quality of life (OHRQoL) in children following treatment under DGA.

pmc-11453080.title: DepActive: study protocol for a randomised controlled multicentre trial of telephone-delivered behavioural activation for the treatment of depression in older adults in primary care
pmc-11453080.creator: Elin Byström, Björn Wennlöf, Inger Johansson, Lena Lönnberg, Marina Arkkukangas, Johnny Pellas, Mattias Damberg
pmc-11453080.description: BackgroundDepression is common in older adults and is related to reduced quality of life and functional ability as well as increased mortality and morbidity. Current guidelines recommend psychological treatments for the treatment of depression in adults. Studies show that about 30% of older adults with depression in Sweden receive pharmacological treatment and about 3% receive psychological treatment.

pmc-11676487.title: Fabrication of an Integrated, Flexible, Wireless Pressure Sensor Array for the Monitoring of Ventricular Pressure
pmc-11676487.creator: Natiely Hernández-Sebastián, Daniela Diaz-Alonso, Bernardino Barrientos-García, Francisco Javier Renero-Carrillo, Wilfrido Calleja-Arriaga, Hongcheng Xu
pmc-11676487.description: This work presents the design, fabrication, and rigorous validation of a flexible, wireless, capacitive pressure sensor for the full-range continuous monitoring of ventricular pressure. The proposed system consists of an implantable set and an external readout device; both modules were designed to form an RCL resonant circuit for passive, wireless pressure sensing and signal retrieving.

pmc-12400465.title: Analysis of 24 pro-inflammatory cytokines in aqueous and serum of 94 patients without diabetes
pmc-12400465.creator: Stephen Jae Kim, Sapna Gangaputra, Jinsong Sheng, Shriji Patel, Archana A Nair, Sara Al Hussein Al Awamlh, John Fitzpatrick, Edward Cherney, Lindsay Veach, Crystal Nicholson
pmc-12400465.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background/AimsTo assess 24 pro-inflammatory cytokines in the aqueous and serum of normal patients without diabetes.Methods94 consecutive eyes of 94 patients undergoing elective vitrectomy surgery were prospectively enrolled. Blood and aqueous sampling were done in the operating room.

pmc-12567854.title: Accuracy and Powder Removal Limits in Multi Jet Fusion 3D Printing
pmc-12567854.creator: Karel Raz, Zdenek Chval, Petra Faitova, Ivan B Meshkov
pmc-12567854.description: Multi Jet Fusion (MJF) is a leading technology for producing functional polymer parts. However, it still faces challenges with dimensional accuracy and removing unfused powder from complex internal geometries. First, dimensional accuracy was mapped by producing 45 identical PA12 specimens on an HP MJF 4200 printer in a 5 × 9 layout across five vertical layers.

pmc-12648975.title: Chronotype in alpha-tACS: Preliminary evidence hints at sleep quality modulation of aftereffects in evening types in the morning
pmc-12648975.creator: Peppi Schulz, Heiko I. Stecher, Christoph S. Herrmann
pmc-12648975.description: Transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) is a promising tool for research on oscillatory brain activity, yet both behavioral and electrophysiological outcome measures show high variability across studies. One source for this variability might be chronotype and an incidental mismatch between chronotype and the time of the measurement.

pmc-12846315.title: Atezolizumab plus Bevacizumab with Transcatheter Arterial Chemoembolization (Sandwich Strategy) versus Atezolizumab plus Bevacizumab Alone in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Multicenter Retrospective Study
pmc-12846315.creator: Ko Hashimoto, Tomokazu Kawaoka, Tomoaki Emori, Aiko Tanaka, Yuki Shirane, Ryoichi Miura, Yasutoshi Fujii, Hikaru Nakahara, Kenji Yamaoka, Shinsuke Uchikawa, Hatsue Fujino, Atsushi Ono, Eisuke Murakami, Daiki Miki, C. Nelson Hayes, Akira Hiramatsu, Kei Amioka, Michihiro Nonaka, Yasuyuki Aisaka, Kei M
pmc-12846315.description: IntroductionThis study aimed to evaluate the effect of sandwiching on-demand transcatheter arterial chemoembolization (TACE) during atezolizumab (Atezo) and bevacizumab (Bev) therapy on overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) in patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).MethodsWe retrospectively analyzed 398 patients who started Atezo/Bev therapy between October 2020 and April 2024.

pmc-12997530.title: Researcher population pyramids: Tracking demographic and gender trajectories across countries
pmc-12997530.creator: Kazuki Nakajima, Takayuki Mizuno
pmc-12997530.description: The sustainability of the academic ecosystem relies on researcher demographics and gender balance, yet assessing these dynamics in a timely manner for policy is challenging. Here, we propose a researcher population pyramid framework for tracking demographic and gender trajectories across countries using publication data.

pmc-13131360.title: A Model to Assess the Costs and Consequences of Changes in Diet and Nutrition From Potential Population-Wide Policies: The Microsimulation of Nutrition, Diabetes, and Cardiovascular Disease (MONDAC)
pmc-13131360.creator: Benjamin T. Allaire, Thomas Hoerger, Rainer Hilscher, Matthew B. Kaufmann, Simon Neuwahl, Lindsay M. Jaacks, Stephen Onufrak, Karen R. Siegel, Hui Shao, Michael Laxy, Ping Zhang
pmc-13131360.description: IntroductionThe prevalence of diabetes continues to increase — more than 38 million people in the US now have diabetes and 84 million have prediabetes. Because many new cases of incident diabetes may be attributed to suboptimal dietary quality, novel programs and policies to encourage healthy eating choices represent promising population-level approaches to reduce the number of new cases of diabetes.
